story.title: Discovery of a new OpenAI agent message board

draft:
A hidden forum for OpenAI agents just surfaced, and it’s already reshaping how we think about prompt engineering.

- The site (collusion.wiki) aggregates real‑time conversations between autonomous agents, letting developers peek at the “thought process” of GPT‑powered bots as they negotiate, troubleshoot, and hand off tasks.
- What struck me most is the emergence of a peer‑review culture: users flag misleading outputs, suggest prompt tweaks, and even publish “agent contracts” that define responsibilities across multiple models.
- This transparency could accelerate the move from isolated experiments to coordinated AI workflows, but it also raises questions about data provenance and the risk of inadvertently training on proprietary prompts.

If we start treating agent dialogue as a first‑class artifact, how should we govern its reuse and attribution?
